## Background

The technical assistance responds to a request from the Tunisian authorities for support on the compilation of air emissions accounts. It is part of the climate statistics programme of the IMF Statistics Department and involves the National Institute of Statistics (INS) and the relevant ministries.

In June 2026, Tunisian representatives took part in a three-day virtual workshop on energy and air emissions accounts. The workshop covered the System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA) framework, energy balances and energy accounts, air emissions inventories and accounts, data requirements and compilation issues [@seea2014; @seeaenergy2019; @eurostat2015aea]. The Tunisian participants presented their work and data [@bouazizi2026; @besbes2026].

## The energy and emissions statistical system

The National Observatory of Energy and Mines (ONEM), under the ministry in charge of energy, produces the national energy balance. Tunisia has compiled a balance since the 1980s and has published it every year in the Eurostat and International Energy Agency format since 2010 [@bouazizi2026]. The INS compiles and disseminates official statistics, including energy indicators and the national accounts.

The National Agency for Energy Conservation (ANME) coordinates the national greenhouse gas inventory for the energy and industrial processes sectors. The Ministry of Agriculture coordinates agriculture and land use, and the National Sanitation Office (ONAS) coordinates waste. The inventory covers 1990 to 2022, with an estimate for 2023, follows the 2006 IPCC Guidelines and uses the global warming potentials of the Fifth Assessment Report [@besbes2026; @ipcc2006].

The INS reported three difficulties at the workshop [@bouazizi2026]. The classifications of the energy balance and of economic activities are not always harmonised. Energy consumption by product and by sector has gaps and relies on estimates. The national accounts cover the informal sector, while the balance does not.

## Data provided

The authorities provided the files summarised in @tbl-donnees. They are kept unchanged in the `data/sources/` folder of the repository.

| Source | Content | Years | Unit |
|:---------------|:-----------------------------------|:-----------|:-----------|
| Energy balance | National energy balance, one sheet per year | 2015 to 2022 | ktoe |
| GHG inventory | Common reporting tables (CRT), Fifth Assessment Report global warming potentials | 2015 to 2022 | kt and kt CO~2~ eq. |
| GHG inventory | Extract of the UNFCCC database for Tunisia | 2015 to 2022 | kt |
| National accounts | Supply and use tables at current prices | 2015 to 2023 | million dinars |

: Data provided by the Tunisian authorities {#tbl-donnees}

## IMF tools

The IMF has developed two tools for these accounts. The PEFA Converter transforms an energy balance into physical energy supply and use tables using a concordance matrix between balance flows and industries [@imf2024pefa]. The I2A converter transforms an emissions inventory into air emissions accounts by economic activity, with a residence adjustment for air and water transport. Both tools combine an Excel workbook with Python functions.

The processing pages of this site follow the same steps in documents that describe each operation and its code.

## Mission programme

The mission takes place in Tunis from 7 to 11 December 2026. @tbl-programme lists the topics planned for each day.

| Day | Topics |
|:-----------|:------------------------------------------------|
| Monday 7 December | Opening meeting with the INS Director General. Objectives, scope and expected deliverables. National statistical system and progress in implementing the SEEA. Institutional arrangements for energy statistics. Demonstration of the PEFA and AEA tools. |
| Tuesday 8 December | Energy accounts framework: activity and product classifications, allocation matrix, residence and territory adjustment, consistency checks. Compilation and dissemination of energy accounts. |
| Wednesday 9 December | Institutional arrangements and data sources for air emissions accounts. Air emissions accounts framework: activity and source classifications, allocation matrix, residence and territory adjustment, consistency checks. Compilation and dissemination. |
| Thursday 10 December | Dissemination formats and indicators. INS workplan on energy and air emissions accounts. Drafting of the technical assistance report and meetings with partners. |
| Friday 11 December | Discussion of the draft report, recommendations and roadmap. Presentation of the recommendations. Pending discussions. |

: Mission programme {#tbl-programme}
